contract.reader: A firmware developer who has outgrown the superloop (entries 1 and 2) and must decide whether a set of periodic jobs will meet its deadlines under an RTOS
contract.problem: Structuring firmware as prioritized tasks and proving, before the system is built, that every task meets its deadline in the worst case, including the effect of shared resources and interrupts
contract.outcome: Explain task states, context switches and periodic release with delay-until; assign rate- or deadline-monotonic priorities; apply the Liu and Layland bound and know when it is inconclusive; compute response times by iteration, with blocking; recognize priority inversion and bound it with inheritance or ceilings; fold ISR load into the analysis
contract.contribution: One three-task example carried from the utilization bound through response-time analysis, a schedule simulation that confirms the computed response time, a fixed-priority versus EDF counterexample, and a worked design that ties the ISR cost of entry 2 into the analysis
contract.evidence: Worked arithmetic; three Python programs with real output (re-run in the live review); Liu and Layland (1973), Leung and Whitehead (1982), Joseph and Pandya (1986), Audsley et al. (1993), Sha et al. (1990), Davis et al. (2007), Burns and Wellings (2009), Buttazzo (2011), IEEE Std 1003.1-2017, Reeves (1997)
contract.limitations: Single-core, fixed-priority analysis with deadlines no longer than periods and no self-suspension; kernel overheads only folded into C_i; no particular kernel API

findings.problem: The diagram has no caption, and at 360 px the Blocked state is cut at the right edge with no scroll cue
findings.whyItMatters: Blocked is the state that distinguishes an RTOS task from busy-waiting; a caption would name what to notice
findings.action: Add a caption; consider a layout that fits at 360 px
findings.acceptance: facts.json of new captures reports 0 SVG figures without a title and the Blocked state is visible at 360 px or a scroll cue shows

findings.location: Section 2.5 and Section 3.4, possessives after inline math (desktop-light-13 and 16; mobile-light-23, 28 to 30)
findings.problem: Five possessives after a math symbol render with a left quotation mark (tau‘s) instead of an apostrophe
findings.whyItMatters: Typographic polish; the mark reads as an opening quote
findings.action: Write ’ after the math or rephrase (the first job of tau_2), preferably fixed site-wide
findings.acceptance: No left quotation mark after inline math on new captures
